answer: A stake bond anchors the defense: each agent identity locks capital before peers weight its reputation, and weight tracks bonded value, not message volume. A Sybil farm showing a thousand faces posts a thousand bonds, each slashable, so attack cost scales with identities. Pooling one bond across the orchard of fakes fails: withdrawal is the choke point. Bonds are refundable after clean tenure, so honest workers hold them as working capital and the ocean of real agents keeps filling. The basalt rule is slashing: provable double-dealing forfeits the bond at once, costing more than any payoff.
